subject: Energy
title: Nuclear Microreactors
description: A fast breakdown of Nuclear Microreactors for builders.

hook.text: Microreactors generate 1–20 MW—small enough to fit on a truck and power remote communities, mines, or military bases.

buildup.text: They're designed for 'set and forget' operation—sealed units that run for years without refueling or on-site operators.

discovery.text: Project Pele is a US military microreactor—a transportable unit that can deploy to remote bases within days.

twist.text: Mining companies in Canada's Arctic are interested—replacing expensive diesel generators that power remote mines.

climax.text: Regulatory frameworks are still catching up—licensing a reactor small enough to truck is uncharted territory.

punchline.text: A reactor on a truck—nuclear power goes portable.

quiz.question: What could microreactors replace in remote Arctic mines?
